Benchmark parity vs existing hosted provider
notes: Background: NimblePatch builds an IDE-integrated copilot used by internal developer teams and paying customers.
Primary ask: robust, auditable model/version pinning for reproducible code completions across releases.
They run nightly unit-test based evals (repo-level tests + linting) against model outputs; need gates that prevent rollouts that increase test-suite failures.
Latency requirement: p95 < 120ms for single-file completions; p99 target < 250ms for streaming incremental tokens.
Throughput target: sustained ~150 streaming sessions concurrent during team peak; burst to 400+ sessions with graceful degradation.
Cost sensitivity: medium-high. Will trade small latency increase for 4-8x cost savings via quantized model variants, but need clear regressions alerts.
Model preferences: open-code oriented models (StarCoder-like, CodeLlama family) with quantized variants; preference for ability to pin to exact model hash and runtime kernel config.
Routing/fallback: prefer automatic fallback to a cheaper quantized variant for non-critical teams, and canary split for core teams. Must support sticky session routing for UX consistency.
Security/compliance: customer-managed KMS for keying, SSO via SAML, audit logs pushed to their SIEM, data residency in us-east-1 for EU-sensitive projects.
Notes from 2026-02-14 call: 'We need deterministic canaries — if a model change causes 0.5% uplift in failing unit tests we must automatically halt.' — VP Eng.
PM comment: wants an "eval gate" UI that shows per-prompt regression deltas and a single-click rollback to previous pinned model.

Proposed POC: Redwood to provision dedicated pool with two pinned variants (v1.3 quantized & v1.2 baseline), run 14-day canary on 5% traffic, ship evaluation reports daily (unit-pass rate, latency, token cost).
Action items: SE (Diego) to deliver canary config template; infosec to provide VPC egress rules; NimblePatch to provide three canonical repos and test harness by 2026-03-17.
Risk: their internal CI is flaky; need to isolate metric noise vs real model regressions (suggest A/B with synthetic deterministic prompts).
